questions.q: Which cost is explicitly modeled as negligible and deliberately ignored?
options: Commission
Short borrow fee
Cash drag / margin interest
Market impact
questions.explain: Cash drag and margin interest are noted as immaterial and deliberately left out of the cost model — not every cost is worth modeling.

questions.q: How does the square-root market impact model behave as participation rate increases?
options: Impact decreases as participation increases
Impact stays constant regardless of participation
Impact scales with the square root of the participation rate, so it grows nonlinearly as trade size relative to ADV increases
Impact only applies to the long leg
questions.explain: impact = 0.1 × daily volatility × sqrt(participation rate) — impact grows with the square root of participation, accelerating as trades get larger relative to ADV.

questions.q: What happens to SR-5's Sharpe ratio when going from gross to net of costs over 2012–2025?
options: It stays the same at 0.76
It falls from 0.76 to 0.42 — roughly cut in half
It improves from 0.42 to 0.76
It turns negative
questions.explain: Gross Sharpe of 0.76 falls to a net Sharpe of 0.42, roughly half, driven by the strategy's high turnover.

questions.q: Why does weekly turnover of about 85% of notional matter so much for net performance?
options: It has no effect on net performance, only on holdings-log size
Annualized to roughly 44x per year, it multiplies small per-trade costs into a large cumulative annual drag
It only affects the short leg's borrow fee
It determines the VIX regime overlay's scaling factor
questions.explain: ~85% weekly turnover annualizes to ~44x per year; trading that much of the book repeatedly accumulates costs that roughly halve net Sharpe versus gross.

questions.q: What is the estimated AUM capacity for SR-5 before net Sharpe erodes below about 0.2, and what's the binding constraint?
options: $1.5B AUM, constrained by SPY's liquidity
$150M AUM, constrained by the lower-ADV names XLC and XLRE hitting the participation cap first
$15M AUM, constrained by commission costs alone
No capacity limit exists for a dollar-neutral strategy
questions.explain: Capacity is estimated at roughly $150M AUM, with XLC and XLRE's lower average daily volume as the binding constraint that hits the 5%-of-ADV participation cap first.
